tldr: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2—up to 30% faster than 5.1, priced $8/$40, scoring 65 on Artificial Analysis—and a fast mode at $16/$80 that delivers 2.5x the tokens/sec. Meta launched Muse Ember, a small model built for agent work with a 1M token window. Strong agent memory and GraphRAG research from the overnight arXiv.

models.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
models.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic's most capable model, with gains over Fable 5.1 in coding, reasoning, and vision. Up to 30% faster generation, $8/$40 per million tokens (down from $10/$50), and a fast mode at $16/$80 delivering 2.5x the output speed.
models.why: Fable 5.2 is the strongest reasoning model on the market. We use Opus 5.5 daily, but Fable runs the hardest technical builds—autonomous agent work, multi-session debugging, and the wehshi PR review panel. The speed and price gains mean switching costs less and waits less.

models.title: Muse Ember: Our smallest, most efficient model
models.summary: Meta launched Muse Ember, their smallest and most efficient model, designed for complex reasoning execution and agent workflows—tool calls, coding subtasks, routing—with a 1M-token context window, at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens.
models.why: Muse Ember's pricing and 1M context fit the subagent and tool-loop role in our harnesses. If it handles iterative grounding and tool calls reliably, it can run the repetitive agent work while Opus or Fable handles the plan.

models.title: Nex AGI: Nex-N2.6
models.summary: Nex AGI released Nex-N2.6, a 321B-parameter agentic model built on GLM-5.3-Flash, suited for computer use, coding, and long-horizon tasks with tools, at $0.12/$0.40 per million tokens.
models.why: Nex-N2.6 claims computer-use capability at near-Ember pricing. Worth probing on tool-heavy agent loops and SalesKick's grading harness if it can replace higher-cost models on structured agentic flows.

models.title: Thinking Machines: Inkling 2 Small (free)
models.summary: Thinking Machines Lab launched Inkling 2 Small, a multimodal mixture-of-experts reasoning model with 17B active parameters out of 594B total, with a 1M token context—free on OpenRouter.
models.why: A free multimodal reasoning model with a 1M context is a zero-cost probe for vision-heavy work like document extraction for EverRaise or visual grading experiments in SalesKick.

research.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
research.summary: This paper compares conversational memory strategies—retrieval-augmented generation versus compaction into atomic facts—on the LoCoMo benchmark (1,985 questions), showing that both arms return comparable results against the same stores with the same generator.
research.why: Mnemosyne uses compaction (working memory to episodic summaries). This eval validates the compaction path against naive RAG, and the same-store design means we can benchmark our own approach without rebuilding the harness.

research.title: Typed-Centrality Grounding for Agentic GraphRAG: A Symbolic Approach for Agentic Reasoning
research.summary: Typed-Centrality Grounding introduces a symbolic approach for agentic GraphRAG that retrieves relevant subgraphs via typed centrality scoring, improving structured context provision to LLMs for knowledge-graph-backed reasoning.
research.why: EverRaise and Mackinac use hybrid retrieval (vector + metadata + graph). Typed-centrality grounding offers a sub-quadratic way to rank subgraphs for context, which directly addresses our 'how much of the graph fits in the prompt' problem.

research.title: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation
research.summary: This paper proposes a multi-agent architecture with LLM-based orchestration for conversational recommendation, integrating memory, retrieval, and decision-making across sessions rather than treating each session in isolation.
research.why: SalesKick's coaching loop and EverRaise's multi-turn voice flows are conversational agents that need memory across sessions. The orchestration pattern here—multiple specialized agents with shared memory—maps to our subagent harness.

research.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
research.summary: MemoryDojo benchmarks agent memory poisoning: malicious instructions stored in one session propagate through memory systems and are retrieved and executed in later sessions. The benchmark tests how memory architectures differ in vulnerability.
research.why: Every agent with a cross-session memory is vulnerable to this. Mnemosyne's BEAM tiering and validator hooks are partial defenses, but this benchmark gives us a structured way to probe the attack surface and tighten the gates.

releases.title: langchain-core==1.7.7
releases.summary: LangChain Core 1.7.7 caps nesting depth in `load()` and patches security lock resolutions for newer Python versions.
releases.why: We use LangChain in the Mackinac retrieval pipeline. The nesting-depth cap is a safety guardrail; worth pulling into the next dependency refresh.

releases.title: v4.77.0
releases.summary: Langfuse v4.77.0 removes automatic tokenization (deprecated, no one should depend on it), adds proper Topics cost tracking, Amazon Bedrock upstream with API key auth, and runs per-trace Topics summaries on a dedicated queue.
releases.why: We use Langfuse for tracing SalesKick and EverRaise agent runs. The Topics queue change is a performance gain when trace volume is high; the Bedrock upstream matters if we route any calls through their gateway.

releases.title: v16.4.6
releases.summary: Next.js v16.4.6 pins Tailwind to 4.3.3, compresses route handler responses automatically, and includes Turbopack garbage collection fixes for dev builds.
releases.why: SalesKick and Pipeline's client dashboards run Next. The route-handler compression is a free bandwidth win; the Turbopack GC fix addresses the long-session memory leak we hit in local dev.

hackernews.title: Is Opus 5.5 nerfed? Thinking patterns changed on November 3
hackernews.summary: A thread claiming Opus 5.5 was nerfed on November 3 based on observed thinking-pattern changes (768 points, 483 comments). The discussion surfaces no official confirmation from Anthropic.
hackernews.why: We run Opus 5.5 on the daily agent loop and wehshi reviews. If there was a behavior change, we'd see it in the panel verdicts and the vault ingest quality. Worth a calibration check against our own panel logs.

hackernews.title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
hackernews.summary: A GitHub repo documenting that Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators (479 points, 114 comments). The discussion covers privacy implications and the AI training feedback loop.
hackernews.why: If we ever integrate Gemini into a client flow, this is a hard privacy boundary. The GitHub evidence means we reference this thread when evaluating vendor data policies for SalesKick and EverRaise.

hackernews.title: TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max
hackernews.summary: Google announced TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, new cloud TPU generations (228 points, 71 comments). The HN thread debates cost, availability, and whether TPUs still matter in the GPU-dominated market.
hackernews.why: We run inference on OpenRouter and occasionally bare GPUs. TPUs are a non-option for us today, but the 8i Max generation is Google's answer to H200 and B200; worth knowing when the cost comparison flips.

hackernews.title: The same H100 costs $2.69 or $12.29 an hour depending where you rent it
hackernews.summary: A data-receipts analysis showing H100 hourly rates vary from $2.69 to $12.29 depending on provider (168 points, 85 comments). The thread surfaces which providers offer the low end and what the catch is.
hackernews.why: If we ever need bare GPU time for fine-tuning or local serving, this pricing map is the starting point. A 4.6x spread means provider selection is not a rounding error.

x_posts.title: ClaudeDevs announces Fable 5.2 availability
x_posts.summary: ClaudeDevs announces Fable 5.2 availability in the Claude Platform and Claude Code, 30% faster than Fable 5.1, priced $8/$40 (down from $10/$50).
x_posts.why: Same Fable 5.2 launch as models and HN. Fastest reasoning model on the market; we switch the editorial-writing profile and the hardest agent loops.

x_posts.title: Which Claude model should you build with?
x_posts.summary: ClaudeDevs posts a new guide on which Claude model to build with, covering when to use Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet, or Haiku, and how to adjust effort instead of switching models.
x_posts.why: Model routing is a first-class problem in our harnesses—what runs the orchestrator versus the subagents, whether we pay for Fable on tool loops or drop to Haiku. This guide codifies the Anthropic-recommended pattern before we improvise one.

x_posts.title: Hermes Cloud agents open in browser tabs
x_posts.summary: Nous announces Hermes Cloud agents now open in a browser tab with the same interface as Hermes Desktop, hosted 24/7 in their own container for scheduled jobs.
x_posts.why: We run Botterfly on pandybot in a headless session with cron jobs. The Hermes Cloud offering is the hosted equivalent; if we need another persistent agent without spinning our own box, this is the path.
